Rashi on Gittin 37a:10:1.hebrew: אינו משמט - דכגבוי דמי, וכמו שהקרקעות בחזקת המלוה הן וגבויות ממש, ואין כאן חוב:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:10:1.english: [The Sabbatical Year] does not abrogate [it] - For it is considered as already collected, and [it is] as though the lands are in the possession of the lender and are actually collected, and there is no debt here:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:11:1.english: He specified for him - The borrower [specified] to the lender:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:11:2.english: One field for his loan - [He] designated it for him to collect from it:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:11:3.hebrew: סיים - הראה בסימניה ובמצריה, דכגבוי ממש דמי:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:11:3.english: Specified - He indicated [the field] by its landmarks and boundaries, for it is considered as though [it were] already collected:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:11:4.hebrew: אפילו כתב כל נכסיי אחראין - דלא דמי לגבוי כל כך כסיים, אפ"ה אינו משמט:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:11:4.english: Even [if] he wrote, "All of my property is pledged" - [Even though] it is not as similar to [already] collected [property] as [when] he specified [a field], even so, [the Sabbatical Year] does not abrogate [the debt]:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:12:1.english: The relative of Rabbi Asi - He was the lender:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:13:1.hebrew: מדמין - נראה בעינינו, וכמדומין אנו כן, ולא שמענו מרבותינו:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:13:1.english: [We] surmise - [meaning] it appears [so] to us and we suppose [it to be] so, and we have not heard [it] from our teachers:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:13:2.english: [Should] we perform an action - [Meaning,] to actively extract his money:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:13:3.hebrew: דבית שמאי - במסכת סוטה (דף כה.): מתו בעליהן עד שלא שתו, בית שמאי אומרים: נוטלות כתובתן ולא שותות כו':
Rashi on Gittin 37a:13:3.english: [The view] of Beit Shammai - In Tractate Sotah (25a): [If] their husbands died before they drank [the bitter waters], Beit Shammai say: They collect their ketubah and do not drink, etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:13:4.english: That stands to be collected - Since it is a valid document and the land is mortgaged by it:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:14:1.hebrew: דתפסי להו בי דינא - והפקרן הפקר, וגבי מלוה לא קרינן ביה "לא יגוש":
Rashi on Gittin 37a:14:1.english: As the court seizes them - and what they declare ownerless is [legally] ownerless, and regarding the lender, we do not apply to him [the prohibition], "he shall not exact [payment]":

Rashi on Gittin 37a:15:1.english: That he holds it - and he does not press him or demand anything [from him]:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:16:1.english: Collateral is different - [collateral] of movable property:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:16:2.hebrew: דקני ליה - למלוה, ואם אבד חייב באחריותו; הלכך כגבוי נמי דמי לענין שביעית:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:16:2.english: That he acquires it - [i.e.,] the lender [acquires it], and if it is lost, he is liable for it; therefore, it is also considered as [already] collected with respect to the Sabbatical year:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:1:1.hebrew: בולי ובוטי - עשירים ועניים; עשירים שלא יפסידו, ועניים שלא ינעלו דלת בפניהם:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:1:1.english: Bulei and butei - The wealthy and the poor: the wealthy, so that they will not suffer loss, and the poor, so that [lenders] will not lock the door before them:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:1:3.english: You shall lend him [ha'avet] - And who are the borrowers? The poor:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:1:4.hebrew: ללעוזא - שאינו מדבר בלשון עברי הוא לעוזא, ואותו ששאל רבא הימנו זאת היה מדבר בלשון פרוזבול, ופי' לו שבלשונו "פרוז" — פורסא, תקנה:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:1:4.english: To a foreigner [lela'oza] - [One] who does not speak the Hebrew language is [called] a la'oza, and the one whom Rava asked this spoke the language of [the word] prozbul, and he explained to him that in his language, proz [means] pursa, [i.e.,] an enactment:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:2:1.english: [Orphans] do not require a prosbol - For the Sabbatical year does not cancel a debt [owed to] their deceased father:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:2:2.hebrew: ר"ג ובית דינו - כלומר, נשיאי ישראל שבכל דור ודור:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:2:2.english: Rabban Gamliel and his court - That is to say, the leaders of Israel in every generation:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:2:3.hebrew: אביהן של יתומין הן - וממונים עליהן ועל ממונם, והיו שטרותיהן כמסורים לב"ד; הא דנקט רבן גמליאל, שהיה בית דינו קיים ונוהג כשנשנית משנה זו, והא דרמי בר חמא ברייתא היא:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:2:3.english: They are the fathers of orphans - and they are appointed over them and over their property, and [therefore] their promissory notes are [considered] as if handed over to the court. The reason he mentioned Rabban Gamliel [specifically is] because his court was extant and functioning when this teaching was taught, and this [statement] of Rami bar Ḥama is a baraita.

Rashi on Gittin 37a:3:1.hebrew: אלא על הקרקע - אם יש קרקע ללוה, דלא תקנו פרוסבול אלא בזמן שהחוב כשאר רוב שטרות שהן נגבין מן הקרקע, דהוי מלתא דשכיחא, כדאמרינן בכמה דוכתי דבמילתא דלא שכיחא לא עבוד רבנן תקנתא. ואע"פ שאינו שוה כל החוב, כדקתני לקמיה "קרקע כל שהוא", האמרן: אפילו מלא מחט גובה מלא קרדום, כמעשה דקטינא דאביי (כתובות דף צא:):
Rashi on Gittin 37a:3:1.english: Only on the basis of land - [meaning] if the borrower has land, for [the Sages] instituted [a prosbol] only when the debt is like most other promissory notes, which are collected from land, as that is a common matter — as we say in several places that the Sages did not enact an ordinance for an uncommon matter. And even though [the land] is not worth the entire debt, as [the Mishnah] teaches further on, "any amount of land," we have said [elsewhere]: even [from land] the size of a needle, one can collect [a debt the value of] an axe, as in the incident of Katina of Abaye (Ketubot 91b):

Rashi on Gittin 37a:3:2.english: And if he does not have - land [belonging] to the borrower:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:3:3.english: Transfers to him - the lender [transfers to him] any amount of land within his field:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:3:4.english: For an oven - to place in it a portable oven or stove:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:4:1.english: Behold, Hillel taught - He was an Amora:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:4:2.hebrew: אלא על עציץ נקוב - שהוא מחובר, וכל שכן על קרקע עצמו אם שלו היא:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:4:2.english: Only on a perforated pot - for it is [considered] attached [to the ground], and all the more so on actual land if it is his:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:5:1.hebrew: האיכא מקומו - דהא מקומו או שלו הוא או השאילוהו לו, הואיל ועציץ שלו הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:5:1.english: Isn't there its place - for its place is either his [own] or it was lent to him, since the pot is his:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:5:2.hebrew: דמנח אסיכי - על גבי יתדות, ואין הקרקע שלו; הלכך נקוב הוי כמחובר, ושאינו נקוב אין כאן קרקע:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:5:2.english: Where [it] is resting on stakes - On top of pegs, and the ground [beneath it] is not his; therefore, a perforated [pot] is [considered] attached [to the ground], whereas [with] an unperforated [pot], there is no land here.

Rashi on Gittin 37a:6:1.hebrew: גידמא - גזע דקל קצוץ, והגזע מחובר בארץ:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:6:1.english: A stump - A cut-down palm trunk, and the trunk is [still] attached to the ground:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:6:2.hebrew: מסרי מילייהו - בלא כתיבת פרוזבול, אלא כך אמר לחברים: "הרי אתם בית דין, וחובי מסור לכם לגבותו כל זמן שארצה":
Rashi on Gittin 37a:6:2.english: They would transfer their matters - without writing a prosbol; rather, [each one] would say to [his] colleagues: "You are hereby a court, and my debt is transferred to you to collect it whenever I wish."

Rashi on Gittin 37a:7:1.english: And to one who is obligated to him, he has [land] - [Referring] to another person who owes this borrower a maneh:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:7:2.hebrew: מדרבי נתן - הוי קרקע לוי, החייב לשמעון, משועבד לפרוזבול של ראובן, המלוה את שמעון:
Rashi on Gittin 37a:7:2.english: From [a statement of] Rabbi Natan - The land of Levi, who is indebted to Shimon, is liened to the prozbul of Reuven, who lent [money] to Shimon:

Rashi on Gittin 37a:9:1.english: That contains a property guarantee - that he mortgaged his lands to him:

Tosafot on Gittin 37a:10:1.hebrew: שטר שיש בו אחריות נכסים אינו משמט - הא דאמרינן לעיל בפ"ב (גיטין דף יח.) דאונס, קנס ופיתוי שזקפן במלוה משמטין, ומפרש דהיינו משעת העמדה בדין, אע"ג דמשעמד בדין גבי ממשעבדי כדמוכח בכמה דוכתי, וכן כתובה משתפגום ותזקוף משמטת אע"ג דגבי ממשעבדי — מ"מ אלים טפי כשמפורש שיעבוד בשטר:
Tosafot on Gittin 37a:10:1.english: A promissory note that contains a property guarantee does not abrogate - That which we say above in the second chapter (Gittin 18a), that [claims for] rape, a fine, and seduction that one converted into a loan are abrogated [by the Sabbatical Year], and [the Gemara] explains that this is from the time of standing in court — even though from when one has stood in court one collects from encumbered [property], as is proven in several places — and likewise a ketubah, once she impairs [it] and converts [it into a loan], is abrogated, even though it is collected from encumbered [property] — nevertheless, [the lien] is stronger when the encumbrance is explicitly stated in a document:

Tosafot on Gittin 37a:15:1.hebrew: דתפיס ליה - פי' בתורת משכון, ודרשי' בספרי: "ולא של אחיך בידך":
Tosafot on Gittin 37a:15:1.english: That he has seized it - Meaning, as a pledge, and we expound in Sifrei: "And not that of your brother [which is] in your hand":

Tosafot on Gittin 37a:15:2.hebrew: אלא מעתה הלוהו ודר בחצרו - אין לפרש דפריך מהלוהו שלא על חצרו, מדלא נקט "הלוהו ויש לו משכון בידו"; אלא פריך הלוהו על חצירו ודר בחצירו, דאפ"ה משמט, כדמוכח בפ' איזהו נשך (ב"מ דף סז:), דאמרינן: האי משכנתא באתרא דמסלקי, שביעית משמטת:
Tosafot on Gittin 37a:15:2.english: If that is so, [if] he loaned [money] to him and lives in his courtyard - One should not explain that [Abaye] is asking from [a case where] he lent him [money] not on [the security of] his courtyard, since he did not state "he lent him [money] and has a pledge in his hand"; rather, he is asking [about a case where] he lent him [money] on [the security of] his courtyard and lives in his courtyard, for even so [the Sabbatical year] abrogates [the debt], as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 67b), where we say: "This mashkanta [mortgage], in a place where they evict [the creditor], the Sabbatical year abrogates [the debt].":

Tosafot on Gittin 37a:16:1.hebrew: שאני משכון דקני ליה מדרבי יצחק - ואם תאמר, והא דר' יצחק שלא בשעת הלואתו, כדאמרינן בהאומנים (ב"מ פב.) ובשלהי פרק הדיינין (שבועות מד.), והכא "המלוה על המשכון" קתני, דמשמע בשעת הלואתו, כדאמרי' התם: והא אידי ואידי "הלוהו על המשכון" קתני, ואין סברא לחלק בין "המלוה" ל"הלוהו"! ועוד, בפרק הזהב (ב"מ דף מח:) ובפ' הדיינין (שבועות מד:) משמע נמי דאפי' בשעת הלואתו אינו משמט, גבי "מלוה על המשכון ואינו שוה אלא פלגא", דקאמר רשב"ג דאינו משמט, פי' מה שכנגד המשכון, ורבי יהודה הנשיא סבר דמשמט, משום דלא תפיס ליה אלא לזכרון דברים בעלמא; והיינו ע"כ במשכון בשעת הלוואתו, דשלא בשעת הלוואתו מאי דמשכן שקיל לגוביינא, ואפילו הכי אם היה שוה המשכון כנגד ההלואה אינו משמט. וי"ל דמסתבר ליה להש"ס: מאחר דקני ליה מדרבי יצחק שלא בשעת הלוואתו, אלים נמי שיעבודיה בשעת הלואה דלא משמט, דקרינן ביה "ולא של אחיך בידך". וכן צריך לפרש בפרק כל שעה (פסחים לא:), דמייתי דר' יצחק גבי ישראל שהלוה לעובד כוכבים על חמצו, דאלים שיעבודיה אפילו בשעת הלוואתו דמיקרי "שלך" לעבור ב"בל יראה", הואיל שלא בשעת הלוואה קני לגמרי; דאפילו מקבל פקדון מעובדי כוכבים, אם מקבל עליה אחריות, מחייב עליה ב"בל יראה". ועובד כוכבים שהלוה לישראל על חמצו, אי הוה קני עובד כוכבים מישראל, לא מחייב ישראל אפי' משכנו בשעת הלוואה, משום דאלים שיעבודיה דלא חשיב מצוי ביד ישראל, דדרשינן "לא ימצא" — מי שמצוי בידו, למעוטי ייחד לו בית אפי' קיבל עליו אחריות, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דפסחים (דף ו.). ומיהו בפ"ק דקידושין (דף ח:) גבי "קדשה במשכון אחרים" דמקודשת ומייתי מדר' יצחק, צריך לומר דדוקא במשכנו שלא בשעת הלוואתו מקודשת; דבפרק האומנין (ב"מ פב.) משמע דלא מהני דר' יצחק להתחייב באונסין, ולא חשיב אלא כשומר שכר, אלמא לא חשיב כשלו לגמרי; א"כ מאיזה טעם נחשב כשומר שכר, אם לא משום דנהנה דקני ליה לקנות בו את האשה וקרקעות או בחליפין? וא"כ, בשעת הלוואתו אינו יכול לקדש בו את האשה:
Tosafot on Gittin 37a:16:1.english: Collateral is different, as he acquires it from [the teaching of] Rabbi Yitzḥak - And if you ask: Surely [the teaching] of Rabbi Yitzḥak applies [only when the collateral is taken] not at the time of the loan, as we say in [the chapter entitled] HaOmanim (Bava Metzia 82a) and at the end of Perek HaDayanin (Shevuot 44a), whereas here [our Mishnah] teaches "one who lends on collateral," which implies at the time of the loan, as [the Gemara] says there: "Both this and that teach 'he lent him on collateral,'" and there is no reason to distinguish between "one who lends" and "he lent him"! Furthermore, in Perek HaZahav (Bava Metzia 48b) and in Perek HaDayanin (Shevuot 44b), it is also implied that even [collateral taken] at the time of the loan does not cancel [the debt], regarding [the case of] "one who lends on collateral and it is worth only half [of the loan]," where Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says that it does not cancel — meaning, that portion corresponding to the collateral — while Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi holds that it does cancel, because he holds it only as a mere memorandum; and this is perforce [speaking] of collateral [taken] at the time of the loan, for [when taken] not at the time of the loan, whatever he took as collateral he took for collection, and even so, if the collateral was worth [the full amount] corresponding to the loan, it does not cancel. And one can answer that it seems reasonable to the Gemara: since he acquires it from [the teaching of] Rabbi Yitzḥak [when taken] not at the time of the loan, his lien is also strong [enough] at the time of the loan that it does not cancel, for we apply to it [the exposition] "and not what is your brother's in your hand." And so too one must explain in Perek Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 31b), where [the Gemara] cites [the teaching] of Rabbi Yitzḥak regarding a Jew who lent to a non-Jew on his leaven: that his lien is strong even at the time of the loan so that it is called "yours" to transgress "it shall not be seen," since [when taken] not at the time of the loan he acquires it completely; for even one who accepts a deposit from non-Jews, if he accepts responsibility for it, is liable on account of it for "it shall not be seen." And [regarding] a non-Jew who lent to a Jew on his leaven: if a non-Jew acquired [collateral] from a Jew, the Jew would not be liable even if he pledged it at the time of the loan, because his [the non-Jew's] lien is strong [enough] that it is not considered found in the hand of a Jew, as we expound "shall not be found" — [meaning] that which is found in his hand, to exclude [a case where] he designated a room for it, even if he accepted responsibility for it, as we say in the first chapter of Pesachim (6a). However, in the first chapter of Kiddushin (8b), regarding [the case of] "he betrothed her with another's collateral," where she is betrothed and [the Gemara] cites [the teaching] of Rabbi Yitzḥak, one must say that specifically when he took it as collateral not at the time of the loan is she betrothed; for in Perek HaOmanim (Bava Metzia 82a) it is implied that [the teaching] of Rabbi Yitzḥak does not avail to make him liable for unavoidable accidents, and he is considered only like a paid bailee, thus it is not considered completely his; if so, for what reason is he considered like a paid bailee, if not because he benefits in that he acquires it [sufficiently] to acquire with it a woman [in betrothal], or land, or through exchange? And if so, at the time of the loan he cannot betroth a woman with it:

Tosafot on Gittin 37a:3:1.hebrew: אלא על הקרקע - משום דמלתא דשכיחא היא שמלוה למי שיש לו קרקע, לפי שאין יכול לכלותו ועומדת בפניו. ואע"ג דעציץ נקוב יכול לכלותו, לא פלוג רבנן במקרקעי. והא דכתבינן אקרקע כל שהוא, פי' בקונטרס משום דראוי לגבות בו כל החוב, כמעשה דקטינא דאביי. ורבינו שמואל פי' משום דקרקע כל שהוא שוה כל החוב, דאין אונאה לקרקעות. וקשה, דהא אמרי' (כתובות דף ק: דביטול מקח יש להם עד פלגא:
Tosafot on Gittin 37a:3:1.english: Only on [the basis of] land - Because it is a common occurrence that one lends to someone who has land, since he cannot consume it and it remains available to him. And even though one can destroy a perforated flowerpot, the Rabbis did not make a distinction among real estate [cases]. And as for the fact that we write [a prosbol] on any amount of land, Rashi explained: because it is fit for collecting the entire debt through it, like the case of Ketina of Abaye. And Rabbeinu Shmuel explained: because any amount of land is worth the entire debt, since there is no [law of] overcharging for land. And this is difficult, for we say (Ketubot 100b) that cancellation of sale applies to them up to half:

Tosafot on Gittin 37a:7:1.hebrew: מדרבי נתן - הלכה כר' נתן, דרבא בפרק כל שעה (פסחים לא.) לא מתוקמא מלתיה אלא כרבי נתן, גבי פלוגתא דלמפרע הוא גובה דאביי ורבא, וקיימא לן כרבא בר מיע"ל קג"ם. ור"ת בתחלה ר"ל דאין הלכה כרבי נתן, ושוב חזר בו, ואין להאריך כאן:
Tosafot on Gittin 37a:7:1.english: From Rabbi Natan - The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Natan, for Rava in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 31a) — his statement can only be established in accordance with Rabbi Natan, regarding the dispute between Abaye and Rava [over whether a creditor] collects retroactively; and we hold in accordance with Rava except for [the six cases of] Ya'al Kagam. And Rabbeinu Tam initially wanted to say that the halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Natan, and subsequently he retracted [this]; and there is no [need] to elaborate here:
